'''Rita B. Zemach''' (née Dresner; April 3, 1926 – June 8, 2015){{r|find|paid}} was an American statistician who worked for the [[Michigan Department of Health and Human Services|Michigan Department of Public Health]], and helped promote women in statistics.{{r|convo}}

==Early life and education==
Rita Dresner started her undergraduate studies at [[New York University]], but transferred to [[Barnard College]] in her junior year.
At Barnard, she became a member of the editorial staff of the ''Barnard Bulletin'', the school newspaper.{{r|bulletin}}
She graduated from Barnard in 1947.{{r|mortarboard|nn}}

==Statistics career==
As Rita Zemach, she became an elected member of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 1961,{{r|nn}}
and earned her Ph.D. in statistics in 1965 from [[Michigan State University]].{{r|msualum}} Her dissertation, supervised by [[Esther Seiden]],{{r|convo}} was ''On Orthogonal Arrays of Strength Four and Their Applications''.{{r|diss}} She later published this work, "the first significant progress on [[orthogonal array]]s of strength 4", with Seiden in the ''[[Annals of Mathematical Statistics]]''.{{r|kiefer}}

Her later research concerned more applied areas of statistics, in health and [[resource allocation]]. By 1979, she had become chief of statistics research and education for the Michigan Department of Public Health.{{r|alum}}

==Recognition==
Zemach was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1987.{{r|fasa}}
